title: Native Hom representative square for every source complex
statement: For the models M of [def-sf-native-weil-closed-models], let χ be a derived Hom comparison satisfying NativeHomRepresentativeCompatibility. For every complex P and K-injective complex I, the forgotten I is K-injective, and there exists an isomorphism from the forgotten native product-Hom complex Hom(P,I) to the ordinary product-Hom complex Hom(UP,UI). Every degree and product projection of its hom equals U applied to the native projection, and the localized comparison square between χ, the two representative model isomorphisms, the factorization of forgetting through localization, and this chain isomorphism commutes. The source P is unrestricted.

source.place: Native tensor model, evaluation compatibility in step 3; Stacks 08J9, 0A97; ringed_forget_normalized_uncurry

proof.text: Instantiate the proved explicit NativeTransport.complexIso at native forgetting and the exact ordinary internal-Hom bifunctor. Its product-projection and source-naturality equations give a canonical comparison for every pair of complexes. On two K-injective complexes, the projection condition in the supplied compatibility identifies its witness with this canonical comparison.

source.place: Native tensor model, evaluation compatibility in step 3; Stacks 08J9, 0A97; ringed_forget_normalized_uncurry

proof.text: For arbitrary P choose a monomorphic quasi-isomorphism P→J with J K-injective. Naturality of the two representative model systems, the factorization of forgetting through localization, the canonical comparison, and χ pastes the square at J into the square at P. Cancel the image of the invertible localized source map. Use the supplied compatibility at (I,I) to obtain K-injectivity of UI. The witness in the conclusion is the explicitly constructed canonical comparison.

lean.statement:
theorem native_hom_evaluation_square_all_sources
    (M : NativeClosedHomModels k₀ l X)
    (χ : M.weilHom ⋙ nativeForget k₀ l X ≅
      (nativeForget k₀ l X).op.prod (nativeForget k₀ l X) ⋙ M.ordinaryHom)
    (hχ : NativeHomRepresentativeCompatibility (ihomBifunctor k₀ l X)
      (ordinaryIhomBifunctor l (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀)).geometricFiber)
      M.weilHom M.ordinaryHom M.weilRepresentatives M.ordinaryRepresentatives
      (Endofunctor.IsoAlgebra.forget (WeilSheaf.frobeniusPullback k₀ l X)) χ)
    (P I : CochainComplex (ProEtaleWeilSheaf k₀ l X) ℤ) (hI : I.IsKInjective) :
    let U₀ := Endofunctor.IsoAlgebra.forget (WeilSheaf.frobeniusPullback k₀ l X)
    let UC₀ := U₀.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)
    let H₀ := ihomBifunctor k₀ l X
    let H₁ := ordinaryIhomBifunctor l (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀)).geometricFiber
    ∃ hUI : CochainComplex.IsKInjective (UC₀.obj I),
    ∃ c : UC₀.obj (CochainComplex.bifunctorHomObj H₀ P I) ≅
      CochainComplex.bifunctorHomObj H₁ (UC₀.obj P) (UC₀.obj I),
      (∀ (n p q : ℤ) (hpq : p + n = q),
        c.hom.f n ≫ CochainComplex.bifunctorHomπ H₁
          (UC₀.obj P) (UC₀.obj I) n p q hpq =
            U₀.map (CochainComplex.bifunctorHomπ H₀ P I n p q hpq)) ∧
      χ.hom.app (op (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P), DerivedCategory.Q.obj I) ≫
          M.ordinaryHom.map (Prod.mkHom (U₀.mapDerivedCategoryFactors.inv.app P).op
            (U₀.mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app I)) ≫
          (M.ordinaryRepresentatives.model (UC₀.obj P) (UC₀.obj I) hUI).hom =
        (nativeForget k₀ l X).map (M.weilRepresentatives.model P I hI).hom ≫
          U₀.mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app
            (CochainComplex.bifunctorHomObj H₀ P I) ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map c.hom
